entry_state: Instrument reductions retain earlier gains and measure later undesignated changes separately. A stopped purchase portion carries its own frozen reserve, whose later release depends on expectation and recoverability. Distinct designation origins cannot be allocated by nominal quantity alone. The inventory transfer now separates basis, cash and profit; the warning that equal final totals can hide wrong interim accounting continues next.
exit_state: Inventory basis transfers precede subsequent sales and recoverable write-downs, without recreating a hedge reserve. Net hedges preserve gross transactions and their different earnings periods. Award expense depends on condition type, settlement rights and current liability valuation. Beneficial amendments retain the original grant cost and add their own service period; cash-to-equity changes follow a separate measured transition. Participation and earnings per share remain to follow.
findings: Partial sales remove both gross inventory cost and the related allowance, so later reversals cannot restore costs of sold goods.
Net currency hedges keep revenue and expense gross and allocate the hedge effect to their respective reporting periods.
Award examples distinguish service and market conditions, cancellation, cash remeasurement, settlement choice and beneficial modifications. No new confirmed defect.
